topology_reasoning.operation: Two identical waveguides begin widely separated, use opposed smooth S-bends to approach over the central interaction region, and diverge symmetrically. Evanescent overlap in the close central region transfers optical power between the guides; coupling is set primarily by the gap and the effective interaction length.
observations: The binary material comprises exactly two continuous, equal-width horizontal guides.
The guides are mirror-symmetric about the horizontal midline and each has a smooth, zero-slope-looking approach/departure.
The material bounding box spans the supplied 18 by 3 um footprint, so the outside guide edges meet that footprint at the ports.
Pixel measurements indicate an approximately 0.63 um guide width, end centre separation of approximately 2.34 um, and a central edge gap of approximately 0.35 um.

function_defining_knobs.coupling_gap: minimum central edge-to-edge gap, controlling supermode splitting
function_defining_knobs.s_bend_amplitude: inward displacement of each guide centre, determining the minimum gap
function_defining_knobs.transition_shape: number of sampled points describing the smooth raised-cosine S-bend centreline

topology_reasoning.implementation: Construct one smooth raised-cosine centreline as a gf.Path and mirror it for the other guide, then extrude both at wg_width on layer (1, 0). This uses only the permitted path/extrude primitive workflow.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitives-only implementation: two 0.65 um gf.Path/extrude raised-cosine S-bends, with 0.30 um central gap, 7.10 um S-bends, and 2.00 um interaction region. The resulting GDS spans exactly 18.0 by 3.0 um.

final.stop_reason: IoU exceeded the required 0.85 threshold on the first visual-metric iteration.
